title: Cabbage & Egg Fried Rice
description: A meatless fried rice with sautéed cabbage, fluffy eggs, and soy sauce.
substitutions: Add mushrooms or frozen peas if you have them.

steps.text: Fold eggs back in and finish with lime if desired.

cookSteps.text: Beat {{eggs}} eggs with a fork.
Scramble the eggs in the hot skillet until just set. Move them to a plate.
Add {{oil}} oil and {{cabbage}} sliced cabbage. Cook until the cabbage is tender-crisp and starting to brown, about 4 minutes.
Add {{rice}} cold cooked rice and break up the clumps. Stir until hot.
Add {{soy}} soy sauce and black pepper. Fold the eggs back in.
Turn off the heat. Add lime juice if using and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
description: Classic low-effort beef stew with potatoes, carrots, and a savory broth.
substitutions: Use frozen pearl onions if preferred.

steps.text: Put everything except cornstarch slurry in slow cooker.
Cook LOW 8 hours or HIGH 4–5 hours.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry at the end.

cookSteps.text: Put the stew beef, potatoes, carrots, onion, tomato paste, garlic powder, thyme, salt, and pepper into the slow cooker.
Pour in {{broth}} beef broth and stir once.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours, until the beef is tender and the potatoes break easily with a fork.
Stir together {{corn}} cornstarch and {{water}} cold water until smooth.
Stir the slurry into the stew. Cover and cook 10 more minutes, until slightly thickened.
Taste the broth, adjust salt if needed, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months.

title: Buttered Cabbage Noodles
description: Tender cabbage and noodles in butter; cheap, comforting, and fast.
substitutions: Add sliced onion if you have time.
A little smoked sausage can turn it into a fuller meal.

steps.text: Toss noodles with cabbage and season.

cookSteps.text: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook {{noodles}} egg noodles until tender.
While the noodles cook, melt {{butter}} butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add {{cabbage}} sliced cabbage, salt, and pepper. Cook 7–9 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Drain the noodles and add them to the skillet. Toss everything together and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a skillet with a small pat of butter.

title: Small-Batch Banana Oat Muffins
description: Six easy muffins for one overripe banana, with oats for a hearty texture.
substitutions: Use quick oats if that is what you have.

steps.text: Heat oven to 350°F and grease 6 muffin cups.
Stir in dry ingredients just until combined.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease or line 6 muffin cups.
Mash {{banana}} ripe banana in a bowl.
Stir in the egg, melted butter, brown sugar, and milk until combined.
Add flour, oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. Stir only until no dry flour remains.
Divide the batter among 6 muffin cups.
Bake 16–18 minutes, until the tops spring back and a toothpick comes out mostly clean.
Cool for 5 minutes before removing from the pan.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days.
